text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian industrial production in 1996 increased by 3.1 percent compared with 1995, official statistics say.
- Director of the British government know-how foundation Stuart Lang says four million German marks already spent for projects in Macedonia, additional two million marks planned this year.

- Social Democrats in the Macedonian parliament to support the government proposal for special law on Pedagogical Academy and classes in the Albanian language in the institution. The Albanian PDP party to vote against the proposal.
- Macedonian Construction Minister Jorgo Sundovski promises Pelagonia workers who are on strike almost one month that their late salaries will be paid and the management dismissed.
- An UNPREDEP vehicle hits and kills a woman in Skopje. Police and UNPREDEP investigating the case.

- The new municipalities established after the first local elections are so poor they have no money for furniture. "In these conditions we cannot even think about any projects," representatives of the political parties say.

- President of the Democratic Party of Macedonia Tomislav Stojanovski from Tetovo demands resignation of the state electoral commission. The reason is that only in Tetovo the new municipality authorities and mayor have not been elected almost three months after the local elections.
